questions.stem: What does 'der Feierabend' mean?
options: The last shift before annual leave
The time after the working day ends
A public holiday in honour of workers
A party held at the end of each week
questions.explanation: 'Feierabend' is the end of the working day and the free time that follows: 'Wann hast du heute Feierabend?' It is not a holiday or a party, although 'feiern' means to celebrate.

questions.stem: 'In vielen Wohngegenden darf man sonntags keinen Rasen mähen.' Which custom does this reflect?
options: Sunday is protected as a quiet day of rest
Lawns may only be mowed by professional gardeners
Sunday is the main day for gardening work
Noise is allowed only on Sunday mornings
questions.explanation: Sonntagsruhe means Sundays and public holidays are kept quiet: shops are mostly closed and noisy jobs such as mowing are frowned on or restricted. Sunday is therefore not a day for gardening work.

questions.stem: What is 'Kaffee und Kuchen'?
options: A dessert course served at the end of dinner
A café chain found in most German towns
An afternoon break with coffee and cake
A breakfast of coffee and pastries before work
questions.explanation: Families and friends often meet in the afternoon, especially on Sundays, for coffee and homemade cake. It is a social ritual, not breakfast or dessert after a meal.

questions.stem: What is 'ein Schrebergarten'?
options: A rented plot in an allotment garden colony
A beer garden attached to a restaurant
A rooftop garden on a block of flats
A school garden where pupils grow vegetables
questions.explanation: A Schrebergarten (also 'Kleingarten') is a plot in a fenced colony of allotments, often with a small hut, where city dwellers grow flowers and vegetables. The colonies are run by clubs with their own rules.

questions.stem: Where does the word 'Schrebergarten' come from?
options: From an old German word for 'vegetable'
From the first gardener of Berlin's parks
From Moritz Schreber, a doctor in Leipzig
From the town of Schreber in Saxony
questions.explanation: The gardens are named after Moritz Schreber, a 19th-century Leipzig physician who promoted fresh air and exercise for city children. The first Schreber association was founded in Leipzig after his death.

questions.stem: What is 'ein Stammtisch'?
options: A table kept for a group of regulars in a pub
The main table at a wedding for the family
A long table shared by strangers at a festival
A dining table passed down through a family
questions.explanation: A Stammtisch is a table reserved for regulars who meet at the same pub at a set time, and also the group itself: 'Er geht donnerstags zum Stammtisch.' 'Stamm-' suggests something regular or established, as in 'Stammkunde'.

questions.stem: 'In Deutschland gibt es Vereine für fast alles: Sport, Musik, Kleingärten und sogar Karneval.' What does this say about leisure?
options: Much free time is organised through clubs
Most Germans spend free time alone
Clubs in Germany are mainly for professionals
Leisure activities are usually run by schools
questions.explanation: The sentence says there are clubs for almost everything, so a great deal of leisure is organised through registered clubs. In Germany, school sport is limited and much youth sport happens in the local Verein.

questions.stem: A pupil says 'Wir haben sechs Wochen Sommerferien.' Her father says 'Ich nehme zwei Wochen Urlaub.' What is the difference?
options: Ferien are school breaks; Urlaub is leave a person takes
Ferien are trips abroad; Urlaub is time spent at home
Ferien last a single day; Urlaub lasts at least a week
Ferien are public holidays; Urlaub is a weekend away from home
questions.explanation: 'Die Ferien' (always plural) are the fixed holiday periods of schools and universities. 'Der Urlaub' is leave from work, or a holiday trip: 'Wir fahren in den Urlaub.'

questions.stem: What is 'das Abendbrot' in many German homes?
options: Bread baked at night for the next morning
A simple evening meal of bread, cold meats and cheese
A bread roll eaten as a late-night snack
The main hot meal of the day, eaten by the whole family
questions.explanation: Traditionally the hot meal was eaten at midday, and the evening meal was a cold 'Abendbrot' of bread with toppings. Many working families now eat hot in the evening, but the word and the habit remain.

questions.stem: 'Im Sportverein duzen sich die meisten Mitglieder, auch wenn sie sich kaum kennen.' What does this show?
options: Club members must always use formal address
Only the youngest club members use 'du'
Using 'du' in a club is thought to be rude
Club membership creates an informal sense of belonging
questions.explanation: 'Duzen' means using 'du'. Saying 'du' to people one hardly knows signals that members see each other as part of one group, so the language reflects the club's shared identity.

questions.stem: 'Laut Hausordnung gilt von 13 bis 15 Uhr Mittagsruhe.' What does the notice ask?
options: Residents should keep noise down in the early afternoon
Residents must eat lunch between 1 and 3 pm
The lift in the building is switched off for the lunch break
Visitors are not allowed in after 1 pm
questions.explanation: 'Die Hausordnung' is the set of rules for a block of flats, and 'Mittagsruhe' is a quiet period around midday. Like Sonntagsruhe, it shows how much value is placed on rest.

questions.stem: What does 'der Freizeitstress' describe?
options: Stress from cramming too much into one's free time
Stress caused by having no hobbies at all
Pressure from an employer to give up one's annual holidays
Worry about the cost of leisure activities
questions.explanation: The compound joins 'Freizeit' and 'Stress': free time so packed with training, lessons and appointments that it becomes stressful. It is often said of busy teenagers.

questions.stem: 'Am Wochenende chillen wir, gehen joggen oder shoppen.' What does this sentence show about the language of leisure?
options: English loanwords are common in everyday talk about free time
German has no native words of its own for any of these activities
Only older speakers use English words in German
These words belong to formal written German
questions.explanation: 'Chillen', 'joggen' and 'shoppen' are English verbs given German endings. German does have its own words ('entspannen', 'laufen', 'einkaufen'), but the loanwords are informal and especially popular with young people.

questions.stem: 'Seit es Streamingdienste gibt, schauen viele Jugendliche kaum noch normales Fernsehen.' What has changed?
options: Streaming services have replaced the internet
Young people only watch TV with their family
Many young people now rarely watch scheduled TV
Young people watch more scheduled TV than before
questions.explanation: 'Kaum noch' means 'hardly any more'. Streaming lets viewers choose what and when to watch, so scheduled television has lost young viewers.

questions.stem: 'Meine Smartwatch zählt meine Schritte und erinnert mich daran, mich zu bewegen.' How does the device affect the speaker's lifestyle?
options: It replaces the need for any exercise
It records every place the speaker visits
It stops the speaker sitting down at work
It prompts the speaker to be more active
questions.explanation: The watch counts steps and reminds the wearer to move ('sich bewegen'), nudging them towards a more active lifestyle. Nothing is said about location tracking.

questions.stem: 'E-Sport ist für viele Jugendliche mehr als ein Hobby; manche Sportvereine haben schon eigene E-Sport-Abteilungen.' What does this show?
options: Only professional gamers are now allowed to join sports clubs
Some traditional clubs now include competitive gaming
Sports clubs have banned gaming among members
E-sport has replaced football in most clubs
questions.explanation: 'Abteilung' is a department or section of a club. Some clubs have added an e-sport section, showing technology changing even traditional leisure structures.

questions.stem: 'Dank Navigations-Apps verirrt sich kaum noch jemand beim Wandern. Andererseits verlassen sich manche so sehr auf ihr Handy, dass sie ohne Akku hilflos sind.' What is the writer's view?
options: Apps are dangerous and should be banned on trails
Hikers no longer get lost because they carry maps
Phones are useless for hiking because their batteries go flat
Apps help hikers, but relying on them too much is risky
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives a benefit, and 'andererseits' introduces a drawback: dependence on the phone. The writer does not reject apps or call phones useless.

questions.stem: What is 'digitales Fasten'?
options: Lowering the prices of digital devices
Using apps that help people to diet
Going without digital devices for a set time
Eating less while working at a computer
questions.explanation: 'Fasten' means to fast, here used figuratively: deliberately switching off phones and screens for a while, also called 'Digital Detox'.

questions.stem: 'Mit dem E-Bike schaffen auch ältere Menschen lange Radtouren in den Bergen.' What does this show?
options: Older people should avoid cycling in mountains
Mountain cycling has become a professional sport
Technology lets more people take part in a leisure activity
E-bikes are allowed only on flat roads
questions.explanation: 'Schaffen' here means to manage. The electric motor helps riders, so people who could not manage long mountain rides can now enjoy them.

questions.stem: 'Früher traf man sich im Jugendzentrum, heute verabredet man sich im Gruppenchat und trifft sich trotzdem.' What is the writer suggesting?
options: Youth centres have become more popular than group chats
Group chats have made young people lonelier than ever before
Technology changed how young people arrange to meet, not if they meet
Young people have stopped meeting in person because of their group chats
questions.explanation: 'Sich verabreden' means to arrange to meet, and 'trotzdem' ('all the same') stresses that people still meet. Only the way of organising it has changed.

questions.stem: In 1988 Steffi Graf won all four Grand Slam singles titles and Olympic gold in the same year. What is this feat called?
options: The Golden Slam
The Triple Crown
The Masters Cup
The Davis Cup
questions.explanation: Graf won the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, the US Open and Olympic gold in Seoul in 1988, the 'Golden Slam'. The Davis Cup is a men's team competition.

questions.stem: Michael Schumacher is best known for which achievement?
options: Winning five Tour de France titles
Winning three Olympic gold medals in downhill skiing
Captaining Germany to a football World Cup
Winning seven Formula One world championships
questions.explanation: Schumacher won seven Formula One drivers' championships, in 1994, 1995 and 2000 to 2004, with Benetton and Ferrari.

questions.stem: Which statement about the basketballer Dirk Nowitzki is correct?
options: He was the first German to win at Wimbledon
He won the Tour de France for a German team
He coached the German team to the 2014 football World Cup
He won an NBA championship with Dallas in 2011
questions.explanation: Nowitzki played his entire NBA career with the Dallas Mavericks and won the championship with them in 2011, when he was also named Finals MVP.

questions.stem: Marlene Dietrich became an international star through which 1930 film?
options: 'Das Boot'
'Lola rennt'
'Der blaue Engel'
'Metropolis'
questions.explanation: In 'Der blaue Engel' (1930) Dietrich played the singer Lola Lola and then went on to a career in Hollywood. 'Metropolis' is Fritz Lang's 1927 silent film, in which she did not appear.

questions.stem: The Austrian actor Christoph Waltz won two Academy Awards for supporting roles in films by which director?
options: Quentin Tarantino
Steven Spielberg
Christopher Nolan
Wim Wenders
questions.explanation: Waltz won for 'Inglourious Basterds' and 'Django Unchained', both directed by Tarantino. Wim Wenders is a German director, known for 'Der Himmel über Berlin'.

questions.stem: The band Kraftwerk, from Düsseldorf, are known as which of the following?
options: Founders of the Schlager style
The first German punk band
A classical string quartet
Pioneers of electronic pop music
questions.explanation: Kraftwerk built their music on synthesisers and drum machines; their album 'Autobahn' (1974) was an international success, and they influenced electronic, pop and hip-hop music worldwide.

questions.stem: The singer Herbert Grönemeyer also acted in which 1981 film about a submarine crew?
options: 'Das Boot'
'Der Untergang'
'Die Brücke'
'Good Bye, Lenin!'
questions.explanation: Grönemeyer played a war correspondent in Wolfgang Petersen's 'Das Boot' before becoming one of Germany's best-selling singer-songwriters. 'Der Untergang' (2004) is about Hitler's last days.

questions.stem: The 2022 film 'Im Westen nichts Neues' won the Oscar for best international feature. Who wrote the novel it is based on?
options: Günter Grass
Erich Maria Remarque
Thomas Mann
Hermann Hesse
questions.explanation: Remarque's 1929 anti-war novel follows a young German soldier in the First World War. Thomas Mann, Hesse and Grass all won the Nobel Prize for Literature but did not write it.

questions.stem: What is the film 'Das Leben der Anderen' (2006) about?
options: A Stasi officer who spies on an East Berlin writer
A family adjusting after the Berlin Wall fell
A young woman racing to save her boyfriend
A submarine crew in the Second World War
questions.explanation: Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck's film, an Oscar winner, shows a Stasi officer who bugs a playwright's flat and is gradually changed by what he hears. A family after the fall of the Wall is the story of 'Good Bye, Lenin!'.

questions.stem: What is unusual about the structure of Tom Tykwer's film 'Lola rennt' (1998)?
options: Lola's 20-minute run is shown three times with different outcomes
The story is told backwards from the final scene
The whole film is shot as one continuous take without a single cut
Each scene is shown from two characters' views
questions.explanation: Lola has 20 minutes to find 100,000 marks for her boyfriend, and the film replays her run three times; small changes lead to very different endings.

questions.stem: What was 'Das Wunder von Bern'?
options: The first Bundesliga match played in Bern
Switzerland winning the European football championship at home
West Germany's surprise win in the 1954 World Cup final
Germany's 7-1 win over Brazil in 2014
questions.explanation: In the 1954 final in Bern, West Germany beat the favourites Hungary 3-2. Only nine years after the war, the win became a symbol of national recovery.

questions.stem: What was new about the series 'Dark' when it was launched in 2017?
options: It was the first series shown on German TV
It was Netflix's first German-language original series
It was the first German television series ever shown in colour
It was the first German series about football
questions.explanation: 'Dark', a time-travel mystery set in the fictional town of Winden, was Netflix's first original series in German and found a large audience abroad.

questions.stem: What is 'das Jugendwort des Jahres'?
options: A word added each year to school spelling tests
The longest new word invented each year
A word banned in schools for being rude
A youth slang word chosen each year in a public vote
questions.explanation: The publisher Langenscheidt runs the vote, and since 2020 young people have chosen the winner online. Winners include 'cringe' (2021) and 'Aura' (2024).

questions.stem: 'Die Party gestern war voll cringe.' What does the speaker mean?
options: It was exciting
It was expensive
It was embarrassing
It was crowded
questions.explanation: 'Cringe' means embarrassing, making you squirm; 'voll' is colloquial for 'totally'. 'Voll' can mean full, which is why 'crowded' tempts, but here it only intensifies.

questions.stem: A teenager writes 'Das Konzert war megaschön!' What does 'mega' do here?
options: It makes the adjective sound sarcastic
It turns the adjective into a noun
It shows the speaker is being formal
It intensifies the adjective, like 'super'
questions.explanation: 'Mega-' is a trendy colloquial prefix meaning 'extremely': 'megaschön', 'megaeinsam'. Such words come and go and mark the speaker as young and informal.

questions.stem: 'Viele deutsche Rapper mischen Deutsch mit Wörtern aus dem Türkischen, Arabischen und Englischen.' What does this reveal about youth culture?
options: Rap is mainly enjoyed by older Germans
It reflects the multicultural backgrounds of many young Germans
German rap is performed only in English
German rappers deliberately reject all foreign influences on language
questions.explanation: Mixing languages in lyrics mirrors everyday speech among young people from many backgrounds, so the music shows how diverse German society has become.

questions.stem: Who was Loriot?
options: A film director famous for horror films set in the Black Forest
A humorist whose sketches mocked everyday German manners
A rapper who mixed German and Turkish lyrics
A footballer who scored in a World Cup final
questions.explanation: Loriot (Vicco von Bülow) was a cartoonist and comedian whose sketches, such as the breakfast egg argument, poke fun at politeness, formality and failed communication.

questions.stem: What is 'der Schlager'?
options: A comedy show broadcast on German television on New Year's Eve
Catchy, sentimental pop, often sung along at parties
Hard rock with loud guitar riffs
A traditional folk dance from Bavaria
questions.explanation: Schlager has simple melodies and lyrics about love and longing; Helene Fischer's 'Atemlos durch die Nacht' is a well-known example. Rock and Volksmusik are separate styles.

questions.stem: 'Die Comedy-Serie nimmt typisch deutsche Eigenschaften wie Pünktlichkeit und Ordnungsliebe auf die Schippe.' What does the series do?
options: It teaches viewers how to be more organised
It hides German traits from foreign viewers
It makes fun of stereotypical German traits
It praises Germans for being punctual and tidy
questions.explanation: 'Jemanden auf die Schippe nehmen' means to make fun of someone. Comedy that exaggerates stereotypes such as punctuality shows how a culture sees itself.
